analysis:
Both changed files are documentation: docs/provider/cli-reference.md and docs/provider/hardware-requirements.md. The supplied head text for cli-reference.md covers lines 843-1760, but the changed ranges are 524 and 527-544, which are outside the supplied excerpts. The only visible change is the scheduler-prefill benchmark row and a new `--prefill-fixed-prompt` flag, and the patch excerpt is truncated. The text I could see in lines 843-1760 (restart, logout, report, unenroll, passthrough env list) reads as already-documented behavior, and I saw nothing that loosens controls. It does not appear to change any code, any gating of DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE, TTL, KEK handling, or any attestation or authorization policy.

hardware-requirements.md adds a 'Flint validation scope' section. It states that there is no new minimum RAM tier, that KV precision must be native, and that the NAX comparison uses build-time and process-start controls. It also says performance targets are not met and earlier throughput samples do not qualify this revision. These statements are conservative and do not overclaim security properties. They do not touch T-041 cache behavior, the TB-011 authorization chain, or the TB-002 wire contract.

Remaining uncertainty: the cli-reference.md diff region at lines 524-544 was not visible, so a benchmark-only documentation change there could not be checked in full. Nothing suggests it affects security boundaries. The new Flint model support is a code change outside this batch, and a reviewer of that code should confirm the Flint model's weight-hash and artifact verification (T-012, T-027) and its KV/prefix-cache handling (T-041). No threat-model update is needed from these docs alone.
